chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Why leaders assembled special all-star players for dates
summary: Teddy Wilson or Red Allen picked players for the sound they wanted rather than the men in their working bands.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: easy. See, because you see what happen was that the best thing about those dates were that all the musicians that were on the date, were all top musicians. And they all knew each other. And at one time had played a gig with each other -- a jam session with each other -- and they all played bands, you know, and worked with different bands. And we all knew what each one could do. That's why when Teddy wanted to do a date or Red Allen wanted to do a date, he say, "Hey, man, I want you to do a date with me." Now he probably got me on this job, but he would pick different other people that people want to do this date. Because this is the sound that he want.
